items.headline: Anthropic set to debut on Nasdaq under ticker ANT
items.summary: Anthropic's IPO is pricing this week with trading set to begin November 19 on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT, with reports putting the targeted valuation around $1.4 trillion. It would be one of the largest tech listings in history and a major test of investor appetite for AI-lab economics.

items.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years
items.summary: Huang stepped down as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO; the company's SEC filing gave no reason, though press reports link the exit to personal-conduct allegations. The move leaves the world's most valuable chipmaker navigating a leadership transition just as it reports quarterly earnings.

items.headline: Alibaba unveils flagship Qwen4-Max model
items.summary: Alibaba launched its largest AI model yet, reportedly scoring near the top of coding benchmarks ahead of rivals like Anthropic's Claude and Moonshot's Kimi, as Chinese labs race to close the gap with US frontier models. The model is not open-weight, though Alibaba says smaller versions are coming.

items.headline: Swiss startup Embodied AI unveils AIR, a cageless factory humanoid
items.summary: Embodied AI, an EPFL spinout, debuted AIR at Humanoid Europe 2026 in Munich: a wheeled, tendon-driven two-armed robot designed to work alongside factory staff without a safety cage. The company says it starts under teleoperation and can transition to autonomous operation on a task within about a month.

items.headline: llama.cpp and ggml reach v1.0.0 after 3.5 years
items.summary: The widely used open-source local-inference libraries hit their first stable release, adopting semantic versioning, an FP8 KV cache and support for over 150 model architectures. The milestone gives developers a formal API/ABI stability promise for building on-device LLM applications.

items.headline: Pentagon renames its AI office the "Super Intelligence Office"
items.summary: The Department of War renamed the Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office (CDAO) to the Super Intelligence Office, following a Trump executive order directing agencies to adopt "Super Intelligence" branding. Officials say the rebrand does not change the office's mission overseeing systems like the Maven Smart System.

items.headline: Google DeepMind introduces Gemini Robotics 2.5
items.summary: DeepMind's new vision-language-action model is aimed at improving robot dexterity and reliability, reporting a 96% success rate in an automotive kitting pilot with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz. The release was paired with an open safety benchmark, ASIMOV-jailbreak, targeting security risks in AI-powered robots.

items.headline: Fireworks AI discloses second breach after cloud-provider hack
items.summary: The inference-platform company said attackers reached its development machines through a third-party cloud provider, exposing account/billing data and, for a limited set of customers, secrets, datasets and partial model weights. Notion confirmed the incident affected AI chat transcripts for a small fraction of its workspaces.

items.headline: New York's RAISE Act opens registration for frontier AI developers
items.summary: New York opened a registration portal run by its new DIGIT office within the Department of Financial Services, requiring large frontier AI developers to register ahead of the law's January 2027 safety-framework and incident-reporting requirements. OpenAI and Anthropic are among the companies expected to face the new oversight.

items.headline: Helsing unveils Clarity, a European military AI targeting platform
items.summary: Defense-tech firm Helsing launched Clarity, an agentic intelligence platform that runs hundreds of AI agents in parallel to turn sensor feeds and open-source data into target recommendations for human operator review. Positioned as a European rival to Palantir's military targeting software, it's designed to run on customer-owned infrastructure.

items.headline: Nvidia guides to $108B quarter in first earnings since Huang's exit
items.summary: Nvidia's fiscal Q3 report, delivered days after Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation, was the first major test of the company's ability to execute under interim CEO Colette Kress, with guidance calling for roughly 90% year-over-year revenue growth excluding China data-center sales.
